slides.title: Hotel rate types, explained in 1 minute
slides.sub: Pick the right rate, pay the right price.

slides.title: Non-refundable.
slides.body: Often the lowest price. But if your plans change, the money is usually gone.

slides.title: Free cancellation.
slides.body: Sometimes a little more. Cancel without a fee up to the deadline shown on your booking.

slides.title: Room only vs breakfast included.
slides.body: Breakfast adds a cost per person, per night. Worth it only if you'll actually eat there.

slides.title: Pay now vs pay at the hotel.
slides.body: Some rates are charged when you book, others at the property. Check before you confirm.

slides.title: Free cancellation on most rooms
slides.body: Compare rate types on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Two prices for the same room on the same night? It's usually the rate type, not a mistake.

Non-refundable is often cheapest but leaves you stuck if plans change. Free cancellation keeps you flexible. Breakfast and payment timing change the total too.

slides.title: How to read hotel reviews like a pro
Sort by most recent.
slides.body: A renovation or new management changes everything. Old reviews may describe a different hotel.

slides.title: Read the 3-star reviews.
slides.body: They're usually the most balanced: what works, what doesn't, without the drama.

slides.title: Look for patterns.
slides.body: One complaint about noise is bad luck. Ten complaints about noise is the hotel.

slides.title: Read reviews from people like you.
slides.body: A couple's weekend and a family holiday need different things. Filter by traveller type if you can.

slides.title: Check the guest photos.
slides.body: They show the room you'll probably get, not the best suite on the top floor.

slides.title: Read the hotel's replies.
slides.body: How a hotel answers complaints tells you how it will treat you if something goes wrong.

slides.title: Found the one?
slides.body: Compare its price on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
A 9.1 score doesn't tell you much. The reviews behind it do, if you know how to read them.

Sort by recent, read the middle ratings, look for patterns and check how the hotel replies. That's where the truth is.

slides.title: Rome: where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 neighbourhoods, 5 very different trips.

slides.title: Centro Storico
slides.body: Pantheon, Piazza Navona, Trevi Fountain. Walk almost everywhere.

slides.title: Trastevere
slides.body: Cobbled lanes, ivy, trattorias and bars across the Tiber. Busy at night.

slides.title: Monti
slides.body: Vintage shops and wine bars, a short walk from the Colosseum.

slides.title: Prati
slides.body: Wide streets near the Vatican, good metro links, quieter after dark.

slides.title: Testaccio
slides.body: A real Roman neighbourhood with a famous food market and classic local cooking.

slides.title: Found your neighbourhood?
slides.body: Compare Rome hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Where you sleep in Rome changes the whole trip.

First visit? Centro Storico. Evenings out? Trastevere. Boutique feel? Monti. Calm and close to the Vatican? Prati. Here for the food? Testaccio.

slides.title: Same hotel, cheaper nights
slides.sub: How flexible dates can lower the price.

slides.title: City hotels often dip at weekends.
slides.body: Business travellers go home on Friday. In many big cities, weekend nights cost less.

slides.title: Beach hotels do the opposite.
slides.body: Leisure spots fill up at weekends. Midweek stays are often the better price.

slides.title: Watch out for big events.
slides.body: Trade fairs, concerts and festivals push prices up across a whole city. Check first.

slides.title: Try shoulder season.
slides.body: The weeks just before or after peak season often bring good weather and softer prices.

slides.title: Shift by one night.
slides.body: Search your dates, then one day earlier and one day later. Compare the totals.

slides.title: Flexible? Compare a few dates
slides.body: Search on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Sometimes the cheapest way to get a better hotel price is to move your dates, not your hotel.

City hotels often get cheaper at weekends, beach hotels midweek. Avoid big event dates and try one night earlier or later.
